pr.title: Publish a summary as a call of its own and tell a refused publish from a missing rule
pr.head: b4b2677985a56d6580b3b5ced92c3d67fe654382

summary: Projector publishes a pull request summary with project summary publish, which pushes the summary to the repository's own Projector site. A host's automatic approval, such as Codex's approval reviewer, can refuse that command as sending repository content to another host unless the user's rules allow it. project init writes those rules into ~/.claude/settings.json and ~/.codex/rules/projector.rules.

In the case this change fixes, Codex refused a publish although the rule was installed. Codex checks each command of a shell chain, such as gh repo view … && project summary publish …, on its own and takes the strictest result. So the visibility check, which no rule names, sent the whole call to the reviewer. The skill then told the user to run project init, which rewrote a rule that was already there.

1. The skill runs the publish alone. summarize-pr runs project summary publish as a call of its own, with nothing joined to it and no visibility check before it. A new --checkout option on summary publish and on summary init --from-published lets an agent whose shell is outside the checkout run the whole summary flow without a cd.
  2. A refusal gets a diagnosis. project review rules --json gains a per-file summary_publish field. A refusal of the lone publish leads to project init only when that field says the rule is missing, both in the subagent and in the session it reports to.
  3. A refusal stops one head only. review-pr keeps summarizing later heads and reports each one as published or blocked.

No allow or ask rule changes. The earlier review's two findings, a publish that could not run from outside the checkout and a session-level instruction that still named project init, are both fixed at this head.

cards.title: Terms on this page
cards.html:
• Allow rule: a line in the user's Claude Code settings or Codex rules that lets a command run without approval.
  • Chain: several commands in one shell call, joined by &&, ;, or |.
  • summary_publish: the new per-file field that is true when the file allows project summary publish.
  • Stale file: a rules file an earlier release wrote, which lacks newer rules but may still allow the publish.

groups.title: Report whether each file allows the publish
groups.kicker: A new field in project review rules --json, and a clearer stderr note for a stale Codex file
intro: project review rules already reported whether each of the user's rule files holds all of Projector's current rules. A file can lack newer rules and still allow project summary publish. That is the case where running init again changes nothing for a refused publish. So the command now also reports, per file, whether the file allows the publish.

For Claude Code, the publish is allowed when permissions.allow holds Bash(project *) or the older Bash(project summary publish *). For Codex, codex_allows parses each prefix_rule pattern Projector wrote and checks whether it matches a prefix of project summary publish.

checks.text: No allow or ask rule changed. ALLOW, ASK, CODEX_ALLOW and the generated CODEX_RULES are the same as at the base, so the change gives no command more access.

files.note: Adds codex_rules_path, codex_allows and publish_allowed, and a stale Codex file's note now says when the file still allows the publish.

checks.text: The regex in codex_allows parses every layout of projector.rules that Projector has written since its first Codex rule, both multi-line and one-line. I checked this against each earlier release's permissions.py.

The keys of publish_allowed are the same shown paths that allow_commands reports, including under CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR and CODEX_HOME. So the CLI's lookup by entry.path finds each file. A file that cannot be read, is not JSON, or has the wrong shape reports false.

files.note: Adds summary_publish to each file entry in review rules --json. Also adds a --checkout option to summary publish and to summary init --from-published, so either command can work in a checkout other than the caller's directory.

checks.text: init --from-published passes --checkout to checkout_root, which runs git rev-parse --show-toplevel there. That is the lookup review setup --checkout uses. Every later git call in the function reads from that root.
The publish runs inside contextlib.chdir(checkout), so the origin check and every git command it runs use the named checkout. --summary and --diff are resolved before the directory changes.

groups.title: Publish alone, and diagnose a refusal
groups.kicker: The summarize-pr, review-pr and review-repo instructions an agent follows
intro: The skills are instructions that agents follow, so a change to their text changes what agents do. summarize-pr now runs the publish alone and drops the visibility preflight, because publish already checks whether the repository hosts a site and keeps a private repository's summary local when its site is public.

When the host refuses the publish, the agent works out why. If the call ran more than the publish, the agent runs the publish again alone. If the publish ran alone, the agent reads summary_publish. When that field is false, the agent asks the user to run project init. When it is true, the agent asks for a new Codex session or for the user's authorization. Either way the summary stays in its work directory and is reported as unfinished.

files.note: The publish-alone rule, --checkout in place of a cd for both publish and init --from-published, and the steps for diagnosing a refusal.

A refused summary holds back only its own head. A review set up with --checkout passes the same option to summary init and summary publish. The session relays the subagent's diagnosis, and names project init only when the rule is missing.
Notes that a file can lack newer rules and still allow the publish, which --json reports as summary_publish.

groups.title: Documentation and tests
groups.kicker: The CLI reference, and tests of the new field, the --checkout option and the skill's publish lines
intro: docs/cli.md describes the new field, the --checkout option, and why Codex sends a whole chain to approval. The tests check the JSON field for Claude Code and for Codex files in several states. They also check that every publish line in the skill is one the generated rules allow and is never joined to another command, and that --checkout publishes from the named checkout.

checks.text: At this head, the full unit suite passed on Homebrew's Python 3.12. project check, claude plugin validate on the repository and on skills, claude plugin test ., and git diff --check also passed.

files.note: Tests that each publish line in the skill passes the generated rules and is never chained. The tests that restated the skill's phrases are gone.
Tests summary_publish for Claude Code settings and for stale, one-line, missing and prompt-only Codex files.

Tests that --checkout works for both publish and init --from-published when the command runs outside the checkout. Also tests that a path that is not a directory is refused, and that init refuses --checkout without --from-published.
